newsitem.title: USA: Quaker's Gatorade faces Q2 challenge.
newsitem.headline: Quaker's Gatorade faces Q2 challenge.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Wednesday cool, wet weather this spring has made for a tough comparison for its Gatorade sports drink in the second quarter.

"Second quarter comparisons will be difficult. Last year it was very hot in the second quarter," James Doyle, an executive vice president who heads the Gatorade business, told reporters after the company's annual meeting here.
In the 1996 second quarter, Gatorade sales rose 14 percent.
"So that's a tough nut to go against," Doyle said. "But I think the sales will come through. We've got very good momentum on the brand."
Gatorade's new "Frost" line, which is being introduced in the United States this year, could account for 10 to 20 percent of the sport drink's domestic sales in 1997.
Overall, Gatorade's worldwide sales are expected to be about $1.5 billion in 1997, up from nearly $1.4 billion a year ago.
Doyle added that, based on industry sales data, the Frost line, alone, is bigger than PepsiCo's All-Sport and Coca Cola's Power Ade beverages.

According to the 1996 annual report, Gatorade had an 81 percent share of the sport beverage market. Quaker has about $5.0 billion in annual sales, excluding the Snapple beverage business it is divesting.
At the annual meeting, Quaker Chairman William Smithburg underscored Gatorade and the company's U.S. and Canadian foods as core businesses that will drive future sales and profits.
He said about 70 percent of Quaker's profits come from U.S. and Canadian foods and about 30 percent from Gatorade worldwide.

Smithburg reiterated the company is reviewing a few, non- core businesses in the international and food service segments of its portfolio. He added he expected the review process to decide whether to sell those units to take about a year.
He declined to comment specifically on the businesses that Quaker might sell. Analysts in the past have said Latin American canned fish and pasta businesses are among the candidates.
